Definition: to make (intrans. be) unsteady, i.e. weak
BiblicalUsage: Chashal is being unsteady, weak, feeble, and it appears once: Amalek smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse is why God remembers Amalek: they struck the weak at the back of the line.
